$comment: What bootstrap-nest.mjs installs into ~/.buzz, and how.
mode     — file permissions. Executables get 0755; nothing here is secret, so
there is no 0600 entry. The .secrets/ directory itself is created
0700 by the bootstrap and never populated from this repo.
resolve  — whether {{TOKEN}} markers are replaced with local-values.json values
on the way in. See $resolveComment below; this is not a blanket yes.
Deliberately NOT in this manifest:
bin/toolbox            154 MB. Fetched from upstream by version + checksum.
mcp/bq-<slug>.yaml     Generated per channel by deploy-claire-channel.sh from
mcp/templates/. Versioning rendered output invites edits
to the copy instead of the template.
.claude/agents/*-<slug>.md  Same — rendered from mcp/templates/agents/.
drive-fence/diag-export.mjs  A one-off investigation into a Drive 403, not runtime.
.secrets/*             Service-account keys. Never versioned, never templated.
$resolveComment: Token resolution is per file, because 'resolve everything' is wrong twice.
RESEARCH_CHANNEL_DATASET_SCHEMA.md is resolve:false on purpose. It is the DDL
source of truth, and deploy-claire-channel.sh substitutes {{BQ_PROJECT}} itself
at deploy time (its sed also handles the per-channel @dataset). Baking the project
in at bootstrap would mean a later `deploy --project other-project` silently emits
DDL naming the project chosen at install time instead.
JANICE_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md is resolve:true and must stay that way. Janice reads it
at runtime for the channel routing table. An unresolved {{JANICE_CHANNEL}} there is
not a cosmetic problem — she would post findings to a channel named after the token.

$comment: THE ONE PIECE THAT IS NOT SELF-SERVICE YET. Read before editing.
The reference binary — the version this stack is known to work against — is
1.8.0 (`toolbox version 1.8.0+binary.darwin.arm64.44d1a05`). It is NOT
fetchable from anywhere this bootstrap can verify:
- The documented GCS bucket (storage.googleapis.com/genai-toolbox) tops out
at v1.1.0. Listing it returns 41 prefixes, highest v1.1.0; v1.2.0 through
v1.8.0 all 404. The URL *pattern* is correct — v0.1.0 and v1.0.0 return 200
— the newer artifacts simply are not published there.
- The googleapis/genai-toolbox GitHub release tagged v1.8.0 carries no assets.
- Buzz.app does not ship it, and it is not installed via Homebrew.
So its provenance is unknown to this script, and downloading v1.1.0 in its place
would silently downgrade the component that enforces the `allowedDatasets` fence
by seven minor versions. That is the last place to take an unforced risk, which
is why the fallback exists but requires an explicit flag.
THE FIX, and it is easy: publish the vetted 1.8.0 binary somewhere the team can
reach, then set `sourceUrl` here. `buzz upload file --file ~/.buzz/bin/toolbox`
puts it on the relay as content-addressed media — the same mechanism the agent
avatars already use — and every operator has relay credentials by definition.
The checksum above is then verified against the download, so a wrong or tampered
binary fails closed rather than half-working.
Until sourceUrl is set, bootstrap keeps an existing matching binary, and
otherwise stops with instructions instead of guessing.
Only darwin/arm64 is recorded, because that is the only platform this stack runs
on: buzz and buzz-acp ship exclusively as arm64 Mach-O inside Buzz.app.
Re-pin with: shasum -a 256 ~/.buzz/bin/toolbox

prerequisites.name: Buzz Desktop
prerequisites.why: Supplies both the buzz CLI and buzz-acp. Neither is distributed separately, and both are arm64 macOS only.

prerequisites.name: claude CLI
prerequisites.why: The runtime every agent is configured against (runtime: claude).

prerequisites.name: node
prerequisites.why: Runs the drive-fence MCP server, the tag-dictionary sync, and this bootstrap.

prerequisites.name: gcloud
prerequisites.why: Only needed to create a new client dataset and service account via setup_gcp.sh.
prerequisites.fix: Install the Google Cloud SDK if you will be onboarding a new client.
